'''Moriyama Hachimangu''' (守山八幡宮, もりやまはちまんぐう) is a Shinto shrine located in Izunokuni City, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|en|Shizuoka Prefecture|qid=Q131320|lt=Shizuoka Prefecture|1=Shizuoka Prefecture}}. It is one of the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} of Izu Province and a successor shrine of {{ill|Iwatokotake Shrine|ja|石徳高神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwatokotake Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (also read as {{ill|Iwato Kotakejinja|ja|いわとこたけじんじゃ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwato Kotakejinja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) along with {{ill|Mugatsuka Shrine|ja|豆塚神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mugatsuka Shrine|1=Mamezuka Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q128867065}}, which is situated in the western, Emma district across the {{ill|Kano River|en|Kano River|qid=Q6364188|lt=Kano River|1=Kano River}}. It is also known as the shrine where {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|qid=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}} rallied his forces and prayed for the defeat of the Taira clan.<ref name="yuisho">(Shrine legend document)</ref><ref name="kk">[https://izunotabi.com/sightseeing/moriyama-hachimangu/ Moriyama Hachimangu] - {{ill|Izunokuni City Tourism Association|ja|伊豆の国市観光協会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izunokuni City Tourism Association|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}</ref><ref name="srg">[https://www.surugawan.net/guide/333.html Moriyama Hachimangu] - {{ill|Izu Suruga Tourism Guide|ja|伊豆駿河観光ガイド|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izu Suruga Tourism Guide|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}</ref>

== Overview ==
The shrine is located in the mountainous area of Moriyama, in the western part of the Terake district (formerly known as {{ill|Nirayama, Shizuoka|en|Nirayama, Shizuoka|qid=Q7039915|lt=Nirayama Town|1=Nirayama, Shizuoka}}) of Izunokuni City. This area is home to a concentration of historical sites related to the {{ill|Hōjō family|ja|北条家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hōjō family|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 北条氏 (曖昧さ回避)|1=Hojo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q398711}} and {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|qid=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, as well as remains of the 【伝堀越御所跡】 from the Muromachi period.

The shrine grounds are arranged in two levels. Immediately after ascending a flight of stone steps, one encounters the stage hall and the haiden. Beyond these, an additional 142 steep stone steps lead to the main hall and another haiden.<ref name="kk"/>
At the lower stage hall, during the annual grand festival in October, rituals such as the Shagiri and the offering of the "Sambansō" are performed.<ref name="rts">[https://www.city.izunokuni.shizuoka.jp/tosikei/documents/nisyu32.pdf Moriyama Hachimangu and the Grand Festival] - Izunokuni City Urban Planning Division</ref><ref name="sbs">[https://www.city.izunokuni.shizuoka.jp/tosikei/documents/2-7nirayama-oohito.pdf Historical Aesthetics of Festival Rituals and Sambansō in the Nirayama-Oohito Area] - Izunokuni City Urban Planning Division</ref>

== History ==
The shrine was founded in {{ill|647|en|647|qid=Q31111|lt=647 AD|1=647}} (the 3rd year of {{ill|Taika (era)|en|Taika (era)|qid=Q1077930|lt=Taika|1=Taika (era)}}), enshrining {{ill|Ōyama Tsumi-no-Kami|ja|大山祇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyama Tsumi-no-Kami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q386563|1=Ōyamatsumi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q386563}}. It later became a Shikinaisha in Izu Province through its association with Iwatokotake Shrine.<ref name="yuisho"/><ref name="srg"/>
In {{ill|907|en|907|qid=Q24163|lt=907 AD|1=907}} (the 7th year of {{ill|Engi (era)|en|Engi (era)|qid=Q1374325|lt=Engi|1=Engi (era)}}), the deity {{ill|Hachiman|en|Hachiman|qid=Q261637|lt=Hachimangu|1=Hachiman}} was enshrined by invitation from {{ill|Usa Jingū|en|Usa Jingū|qid=Q715632|lt=Usa Shrine|1=Usa Jingū}} of Buzen Province and merged with the shrine, which then became known as Moriyama Hachimangu.<ref name="yuisho"/><ref name="srg"/>
In August {{ill|1180|en|1180|qid=Q19702|lt=1180 AD|1=1180}} (the 4th year of {{ill|Jishō|en|Jishō|qid=Q1194671|lt=Jishō|1=Jishō}}), when {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|qid=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}} prayed for the defeat of the Taira clan and rallied his forces, several dozen of his soldiers attacked the mansion of {{ill|Yamaki Kanetaka|ja|山木兼隆|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaki Kanetaka|1=Yamaki Kanetaka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11468747}}, located near what would later become the Nirayama Daikan-sho, and the ensuing flames were observed from this site.<ref name="yuisho"/><ref name="kk"/>
The current main hall was constructed in {{ill|1632|en|1632|qid=Q6865|lt=1632 AD|1=1632}} (the 9th year of {{ill|Kan'ei|en|Kan'ei|qid=Q1192913|lt=Kannen|1=Kan'ei}}) by Sakakibara Teruhisa, the lord of {{ill|Kunō Castle|ja|久能城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kunō Castle|1=Kunō Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q65248350}}, and replaced an earlier structure from 1597 (the 2nd year of {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|qid=Q1328185|lt=Keichō|1=Keichō}}) by the lord of Nirayama Castle, Naitō Nobunari.<ref name="yuisho"/><ref name="sbs"/><ref name="hjs">[https://www.city.izunokuni.shizuoka.jp/tosikei/documents/2-4houjounosato-huuti.pdf Historical Aesthetics along the Old Shimoda Kaidō, as seen in Izunokuni City] - Izunokuni City Urban Planning Division</ref>
The stage hall was constructed in {{ill|1934|en|1934|qid=Q18714|lt=1934 AD|1=1934}} (Showa 9).<ref name="rts"/><ref name="sbs"/>

== Grounds ==
The shrine grounds include:
* Main Hall and Haiden
* Stage Hall and its accompanying Haiden
* A monument commemorating {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|qid=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}’s military expedition
* Torii
